security_audit.summary: The apparent external command finding is a false positive caused by a Markdown code fence. The skill is prose-only, but it contains dual-use red team guidance around evasion, credential abuse, lateral movement, and Active Directory attack concepts.

remediation.issue: Defense evasion content is framed as operational tradecraft.
remediation.suggestion: Rewrite evasion sections as detection engineering checks and defensive validation steps for authorized environments.

remediation.issue: Credential abuse and lateral movement concepts are presented as attack paths.
remediation.suggestion: Add defensive framing, authorization requirements, and detection mappings for each credential and movement concept.

remediation.issue: Ethical boundaries appear near the end of the file.
remediation.suggestion: Move authorization, scope, and data handling requirements to the beginning of the skill.

content.value_statement: Security teams need a clear structure for adversary simulation and reporting. This skill organizes MITRE ATT&CK concepts into planning, detection review, and report guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains the MITRE ATT&CK attack lifecycle at a high level.
Compares passive and active reconnaissance tradeoffs.
Summarizes initial access, privilege escalation, lateral movement, and Active Directory attack categories.
Helps structure red team reports and detection gap analysis.
Lists ethical boundaries and anti-patterns for authorized security work.
limitations: Does not provide exploit code, payloads, or tool commands.
Requires written authorization and a defined assessment scope.
Does not verify current MITRE ATT&CK updates or tool behavior.
Does not replace legal review or security governance.

use_cases.title: Exercise Planning
use_cases.description: Create a high-level plan for an authorized adversary simulation with clear phases and objectives.

use_cases.title: Detection Review
use_cases.description: Map simulated techniques to expected alerts, control gaps, and follow-up improvements.

use_cases.title: Report Structuring
use_cases.description: Organize red team findings into an attack narrative, detection analysis, and practical remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Explain The Lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the MITRE ATT&CK attack lifecycle in simple terms for an authorized red team training session.

prompt_templates.title: Draft A Scoped Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a high-level red team exercise outline for this approved scope: [scope]. Include phases, objectives, safety limits, and reporting needs.

prompt_templates.title: Map Detection Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these simulated techniques to expected detections and likely control gaps: [techniques]. Focus on defensive validation and improvement.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Final Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this red team report draft for clear attack narrative, detection gaps, remediation quality, scope control, and ethical boundaries: [report].

output_examples.input: Explain the attack lifecycle for a security awareness session.
output: The lifecycle starts with reconnaissance and initial access.
Later phases focus on execution, privilege escalation, discovery, and movement.
A defensive review should map each phase to expected controls and alerts.

output_examples.input: Create a report outline for an approved red team exercise.
output: Executive summary with scope and safety limits.
Attack narrative with observed detection gaps.
Remediation plan with owners, priorities, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Review detection coverage for simulated credential attacks.
output: List the credential scenarios that were approved for testing.
Compare expected alerts with observed evidence.
Recommend control improvements and retest criteria.

best_practices: Confirm authorization, scope, and safety limits before using the skill.
Frame each technique as a defensive validation objective.
Document actions, detections, impact, and remediation evidence.
anti_patterns: Using the skill for unapproved systems or accounts.
Treating high-level concepts as permission to perform intrusive testing.
Reporting attack steps without detection gaps and remediation guidance.

faq.question: Is this skill for authorized security work only?
faq.answer: Yes. It should only be used within written scope and approved security testing rules.

faq.question: Does it include exploit code or payloads?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides high-level concepts, planning structure, and reporting guidance.

faq.question: Can detection engineers use it?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help map simulated techniques to alerts, controls, and detection gaps.

faq.question: Does it replace MITRE ATT&CK documentation?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes common concepts and should be checked against current MITRE ATT&CK references.

faq.question: Can it help write a red team report?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines attack narrative, detection gap, and remediation sections.

faq.question: What should users avoid?
faq.answer: Users should avoid unapproved testing, sensitive data retention, production damage, and out-of-scope access.
